about: Today's story on the scanner page (docs/scanner.html): what moved the market each weekday and why, written after the close by a scheduled Claude task. Newest last. Fields: date (the session, YYYY-MM-DD), written (e.g. '7:20pm ET'), headline, happened (a short paragraph), points (2-4 short bullets for the WhatsApp version), matters (one or two sentences), watch (list), movers (list of {t, pct} with pct as a fraction), notes (short tape notes), short (one line for the earlier-days list), sources (list of {name, url}). SPY's close and change, the chart and where the plan stands come from the scan, never from this file. Information only: never part of the plan.

items.headline: The AI selloff deepens on the day Anthropic lists
items.happened: Stocks hit their lows of the day the moment Anthropic's shares began trading: money moved into the new AI stock and out of the old ones. More than 90% of S&P 500 stocks fell, the Dow dropped about 1,100 points and the S&P 500 made its sixth straight loss, 8% under its October record. Asia followed overnight, with Japan and Korea down about 5%.
points: Anthropic's debut pulled money out of other AI stocks
Over 90% of S&P stocks fell; Dow −1,100 points
Sixth straight loss for the S&P 500
items.matters: Doubt about the AI boom had become a broad selloff, not just a tech one.
items.short: AI selloff deepens on Anthropic's debut day; sixth straight loss.

items.headline: Report of an SEC look at Nvidia's accounts sinks the market
items.happened: Reuters reported that SEC staff are looking at possible accounting problems at Nvidia (it said that doesn't establish wrongdoing). Nvidia fell 14% and the Nasdaq 5.3%. The S&P 500 made its seventh straight loss, ending more than 10% under its Oct 6 high, and had its worst week since April 2025.
points: Reuters: SEC staff looking at possible Nvidia accounting issues
S&P 500 10%+ under its high; worst week since April 2025
items.matters: Nvidia had been the market's leader; a question over its accounts hit the whole AI trade.
items.short: Report of an SEC look at Nvidia's accounts; NVDA −14%, seventh straight loss.

items.headline: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia and stocks jump
items.happened: Over the weekend Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, eleven days after he resigned; President Trump said he was personally involved. Nvidia rose 31.5%, adding more than $1 trillion in market value, its biggest one-day gain on record, and lifted the whole market.
points: Nvidia's board brought Jensen Huang back as CEO
Nvidia +31.5%, its biggest one-day gain ever
SPY still closed under the falling line the plan needs to clear
items.matters: The weekend brought relief, which is why Monday bounced, but it fixed only the CEO question, not the SEC one.
items.short: Huang back at Nvidia; NVDA +31.5%, still under the line.

items.headline: The Nvidia bounce fades; stocks give back a little
items.happened: After Monday's jump on Jensen Huang's return, buyers didn't follow through. Nvidia gave back about 6% as analysts said his return isn't the all-clear while the SEC question is open. Anthropic slipped below its $83 IPO price, talk of new US tariffs returned and a report on AI-safety worries hit the AI names again. Outside tech, Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for about $41 billion.
points: Anthropic slipped below its IPO price; tariff talk returned
Sanofi to buy Insmed for about $41B
items.matters: The weekend fixed one problem (the CEO) but not the bigger ones: the SEC question and doubt about AI spending. One good day hasn't undone a seven-day rout.
watch: Wednesday: last full session before Thanksgiving; thin trading can mean bigger moves
Thursday: market closed. Friday: half day (1pm close)
Any news on the SEC's Nvidia look, and on tariffs
items.short: Nvidia's bounce fades (−5.9%); Anthropic below its IPO price.
